sections.heading: Resonant frequency placement
sections.text: Place the resonant pole exactly at the output fundamental (50 or 60 Hz, or the islanded reference frequency). Even small offset produces a steady-state phase error that no proportional term recovers. If the system must track grid frequency, make the resonant frequency a function of the measured grid frequency rather than a fixed constant.

sections.heading: Damping of the resonant peak
sections.text: An ideal PR controller has infinite gain at the resonant frequency, which is unrealizable on a digital implementation. Use a damped form (k_r * 2*ω_c*s / (s^2 + 2*ω_c*s + ω_0^2)) and start with ω_c ≈ 5 to 10 rad/s. Lower damping gives better tracking but reduces the system phase margin near ω_0.

sections.heading: Harmonic compensators
sections.text: For nonlinear loads, add resonant compensators at the 3rd, 5th, and 7th harmonics, each with its own damping. Tune each compensator gain individually — combined gain is not a simple sum because the harmonics interact through the load current. Add them one at a time and verify margin after each.

sections.heading: Discretization
sections.text: PR controllers are sensitive to discretization method. Bilinear (Tustin) with prewarping at the resonant frequency preserves the pole location best. Forward or backward Euler shifts the resonant pole and introduces a steady-state error proportional to the sample time.

sections.heading: Sample time
sections.text: Use a sample time at least 20x faster than the highest compensated harmonic. For 7th harmonic compensation on 60 Hz, sample at >= 8.4 kHz. Below this, the resonant poles alias and the controller can become unstable.
